sources.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2020. Aspects of the phonology and morphosyntax of Kyak, an Adamawa language. Language in Africa 1(3): 373–404. (sister language Kyak/Bambuka, not Burak)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Describes Kyak (bamb1262), a Bikwin sister language: tone-marked throughout; the words stress/accent do not occur in the text. Burak mentioned only in the classification sentence (p. 374 area: 'comprising Burak-Loo, Maghdi and Mak, and a southern subgroup'). Not a Burak source.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Blench, Roger. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2026_12031
sources.note: Ethnography and settlement history; §3.2.3.6 Burak (p. 18) gives population (c. 7,500, 1991 census), clans and migrations; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Othaniel, Nlabephee. 2020. The Jen language cluster: A comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17–99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a comparative wordlist study of ten Jen varieties (Burak included). §3.3 Tone (p. 43): 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted' for the cluster; Burak forms carry H/M/L tone marks throughout (Table 20 p. 44 gives Burak *L reflexes gɑ̀b 'answer', kɔ̀klɛ̀ 'bark'); §3.4 breathy voice. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the 83 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.note: First-hand summary of the sound system (slide 6 'General Features'): c. 24 consonants incl. implosives and labial-velars, nine vowels, syllable shapes (C)V(V), CV(V)C, SVO, and 'Tones: Two level (H, L) with a downstep high tone (ꜜH)'. Data throughout are tone-marked (e.g. tál 'stone' ~ jé tál 'stones'). No fuller tonal analysis (TBU, contours, tone rules) in the slides; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. Bukuru/Jos: Theological College of Northern Nigeria, 83 pp. (B.A. dissertation per Norton & Othaniel 2020; M.A. per Glottolog)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only work devoted to the phonology of the cluster including Burak; a per-language phonology chapter is the most likely place for a suprasegmental (tone, and possibly stress) statement on Burak. Named by the earlier scan and by the Mainz Bikwin-Jen page.

tone.quote: Considering the hierarchical organization of the phonological patterns of languages, this study aims a phonological comparison at the segment level. Furthermore, this research is not aimed at detailed phonemic analyses of all the languages of the Jen language cluster. Rather, it shall be a direct comparison of sound inventories of the languages of the cluster, and the correspondence sets that follows.
tone.summary: Segment-only comparative thesis; no tone statement for Burak. About 100 Burak forms in the cognate tables bear uncommented tone diacritics (acute, grave, macron, circumflex). Nothing on stress.
tone.says: Segment-only comparative thesis; no tone statement for Burak. About 100 Burak forms in the cognate tables bear uncommented tone diacritics (acute, grave, macron, circumflex). Nothing on stress.
